newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Non-Australia bank earnings boost Westpac.
newsitem.headline: Non-Australia bank earnings boost Westpac.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corp said on Wednesday increased profits from its New Zealand operations and its local finance arm helped underpin the 12.9 percent rise in the bank's half year profit.
The profit rise was partially offset by a fall in earnings from its traditional Australian banking group, Westpac said.
Westpac reported net profit rose to A$638 million in the six months ended March 31 from A$565 million in the same half a year earlier.
The result was slightly above market expectations, which ranged from A$595 million to A$620 million.
Westpac said the results from the Australian operations were impacted by the continued compression in margins, combined with the sale of Challenge Bank's Victorian assets and liabilities.

Profit from the Australian banking group fell to A$274 million in the first half from A$308 million while profit from the New Zealand and Pacific regional banking businesses rose to A$149 million from A$88 million.
"The substantial increase in profit is due to the full period impact of Trust Bank New Zealand, coupled with the partial delivery of synergies associated with the merger."
Westpac said the New Zealand profit were also helped by the sale of equity investments.
It said results from the Asian operations have been positively affected by a prior year tax adjustment. Half year profits from the Asian business rose to A$16 million from A$8 million a year earlier.

Fluctuations in profit in its Americas and European units have been influenced by financial market income, it said. Net profit from the Americas rose to A$20 million from A$15 million. In Europe profit fell to A$33 million from A$41 million.

Westpac said intense competition in the retail and business segments of the Australian market reduced margins and net interest income. But this was partially offset by a fall in bad and doubtful debts.

The rise in non-interest income represents a change in Westpac's transactional banking products and property sales, as well as continued strong growth in sales of financial services and the integration of Westpac Life, Westpac said.
In institutional banking contracting margins have reduced net interest income in the transactional services, financing and property finance areas, it said.
"To ensure efficient use of capital, the financing and property finance businesses are pursuing alternatives for securitising and syndicating assets," Westpac said.
Westpac said the rise in profit from its local finance arm, Australian Guarantee Corp (AGC), was due to high growth in volumes of business within the consumer and commercial units.
Just before the local close Westpac shares were two cents down at A$7.49 in a volatile trading session, which saw its shares trade in the A$7.41 to A$7.60 range.
